content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Qui se manducántibus dat spíritus pinguédinem.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius

veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Qui se manducántibus dat spíritus pinguédinem.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Sacris solémniis iuncta sint gáudia,
content.english: At this our solemn feast,

content.latin: Et ex præcórdiis sonent præcónia;
content.english: Let holy joys abound,

content.latin: Recédant vétera, nova sint ómnia,
content.english: And from the inmost breast

content.latin: Corda, voces, et ópera.
content.english: Let songs of praise resound;

content.latin: Noctis recólitur cœna novíssima,
content.english: Let ancient rites depart,

content.latin: Qua Christus créditur agnum et ázyma
content.english: And all be new around,

content.latin: Dedísse frátribus, iuxta legítima
content.english: In ev'ry act and voice and heart.

content.latin: Priscis indúlta pátribus.
content.english: Remember we that eve,

content.latin: Post agnum týpicum, explétis épulis,
content.english: When, the last supper spread,

content.latin: Corpus Domínicum datum discípulis,
content.english: Christ, as we all believe,

content.latin: Sic totum ómnibus, quod totum síngulis,
content.english: The lamb, with leavenless bread,

content.latin: Eius fatémur mánibus.
content.english: Among his brethren shared,

content.latin: Dedit fragílibus córporis férculum,
content.english: And thus the law obeyed,

content.latin: Dedit et trístibus sánguinis póculum,
content.english: Of old unto their sires declared.

content.latin: Dicens: Accípite quod trado vásculum;
content.english: The typic lamb consumed,

content.latin: Omnes ex eo bíbite.
content.english: The legal feast complete,

content.latin: Sic sacrifícium istud instítuit,
content.english: The Lord unto the twelve

content.latin: Cuius offícium commítti vóluit
content.english: His body gave to eat;

content.latin: Solis presbýteris, quibus sic cóngruit,
content.english: The whole to all, no less

content.latin: Ut sumant, et dent céteris.
content.english: The whole to each, did mete

content.latin: Panis angélicus fit panis hóminum;
content.english: With his own hands, as we confess.

content.latin: Dat panis cǽlicus figúris términum;
content.english: He gave them, weak and frail,

content.latin: O res mirábilis: mandúcat Dóminum
content.english: His flesh, their food to be;

content.latin: Pauper, servus et húmilis.
content.english: On them, downcast and sad,

content.latin: Te, trina Déitas únaque, póscimus;
content.english: His blood bestowèd he:

content.latin: Sic nos tu vísita, sicut te cólimus:
content.english: And thus to them he spake,

content.latin: Per tuas sémitas duc nos quo téndimus,
content.english: “Receive this cup from me,

content.latin: Ad lucem quam inhábitas.
content.english: And all of you of this partake.”

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: So he this sacrifice
To institute did will,
And charged his priests alone
That office to fulfil:
In them he did confide:
To whom pertaineth still
To take, and to the rest divide.
Thus angels' bread is made
The bread of man today:
The living bread from heaven
With figures doth away:
O wondrous gift indeed!
The poor and lowly may
Upon their Lord and Master feed.
O Triune Deity,
To thee we meekly pray,
So mayst thou visit us,
As we our homage pay;
And in thy footsteps bright
Conduct us on our way
To where thou dwell'st in cloudless light.
Amen.

content.english: Ant. The Lord brought forth His fruit in the season of His death, * even that fruit whereof if any man eat, he shall live for ever.

content.latin: Psalmus 1 [1]
content.english: Psalm 1 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 1

content.latin: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
content.english: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:

content.latin: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
content.english: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

segments.t: Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.

content.latin: 1:3 Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
content.english: 1:3 And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

segments.t: Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:

content.latin: 1:3 Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
content.english: 1:3 And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

segments.t: Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.

content.latin: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
content.english: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

segments.t: Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.

content.latin: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
content.english: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

segments.t: Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.

content.latin: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
content.english: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

segments.t: Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.

content.latin: Psalmus 4 [2]
content.english: Psalm 4 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 4

content.latin: 4:2 Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
content.english: 4:2 When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

segments.t: Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.

content.latin: 4:2 Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: 4:2 Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.

segments.t: Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
content.english: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

segments.t: Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?

content.latin: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

segments.t: Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

segments.t: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

segments.t: Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

segments.t: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

segments.t: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

segments.t: In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;

content.latin: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.

content.english: Ant. Us, being many, hath the Lord made one body, * for we are all partakers of that one cup, which is not the communion of the blood of bulls, but of God Himself.

content.latin: Psalmus 15 [3]
content.english: Psalm 15 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 15

content.latin: 15:1 Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
content.english: 15:1 Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. * I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, for thou hast no need of my goods.

segments.t: Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.

content.latin: 15:3 Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
content.english: 15:3 To the saints, who are in his land, * he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.

segments.t: Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.

content.latin: 15:4 Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.
content.english: 15:4 Their infirmities were multiplied: * afterwards they made haste.

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.

content.latin: 15:4 Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
content.english: 15:4 I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: * nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.

segments.t: Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.

content.latin: 15:5 Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
content.english: 15:5 The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: * it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.

segments.t: Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.

content.latin: 15:6 Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
content.english: 15:6 The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: * for my inheritance is goodly to me.

segments.t: Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.

content.latin: 15:7 Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
content.english: 15:7 I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: * moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.

content.latin: 15:8 Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
content.english: 15:8 I set the Lord always in my sight: * for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.

segments.t: Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.

content.latin: 15:9 Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
content.english: 15:9 Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: * moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

segments.t: Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.

content.latin: 15:10 Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
content.english: 15:10 Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; * nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.

segments.t: Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.

content.latin: 15:11 Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
content.english: 15:11 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: * at thy right hand are delights even to the end.

segments.t: Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Communióne cálicis, quo Deus ipse súmitur, non vitulórum sánguine, congregávit nos Dóminus.
content.english: Ant. Us, being many, hath the Lord made one body, for we are all partakers of that one cup, which is not the communion of the blood of bulls, but of God Himself.

segments.t: Ant.
Communióne cálicis, quo Deus ipse súmitur, non vitulórum sánguine, congregávit nos Dóminus.

content.latin: ℣. Panem cæli dedit eis, allelúia.
content.english: ℣. He gave them of the bread of heaven, alleluia.

segments.t: Panem cæli dedit eis, allelúia.

content.latin: ℟. Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, allelúia.
content.english: ℟. Man did eat Angels' bread, alleluia.

segments.t: Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, allelúia.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: Absolutio. Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.
Exáudi, Dómine Iesu Christe, preces servórum tuórum, et miserére nobis: Qui cum Patre et Spíritu Sancto vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.
content.english: Benediction. May the Eternal Father bless us with an eternal blessing.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Benedictióne perpétua benedícat nos Pater ætérnus.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: De Epístola prima beáti Pauli Apóstoli ad Corínthios
content.english: Lesson from the first letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Corinthians

content.latin: 20 Conveniéntibus ergo vobis in unum, iam non est Domínicam cenam manducáre.
content.english: 20 When you come therefore together into one place, it is not now to eat the Lord's supper.

segments.t: Conveniéntibus ergo vobis in unum, iam non est Domínicam cenam manducáre.

content.latin: 21 Unusquísque enim suam cenam præsúmit ad manducándum. Et álius quidem ésurit, álius autem ébrius est.
content.english: 21 For every one taketh before his own supper to eat. And one indeed is hungry and another is drunk.

segments.t: Unusquísque enim suam cenam præsúmit ad manducándum. Et álius quidem ésurit, álius autem ébrius est.

content.latin: 22 Numquid domos non habétis ad manducándum et bibéndum? aut Ecclésiam Dei contémnitis, et confúnditis eos, qui non habent? Quid dicam vobis? Laudo vos? In hoc non laudo.
content.english: 22 What, have you not houses to eat and to drink in? Or despise ye the church of God; and put them to shame that have not? What shall I say to you? Do I praise you? In this I praise you not.

segments.t: Numquid domos non habétis ad manducándum et bibéndum? aut Ecclésiam Dei contémnitis, et confúnditis eos, qui non habent? Quid dicam vobis? Laudo vos? In hoc non laudo.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Immolábit hædum multitúdo filiórum Israël ad vésperam Paschæ:
content.english: ℟. The whole assembly of the children of Israel shall kill the lamb toward the evening of the Passover.

segments.t: Immolábit hædum multitúdo filiórum Israël ad vésperam Paschæ:

content.latin: * Et edent carnes et ázymos panes.
content.english: * And they shall eat the flesh, and unleavened bread.

content.latin: ℣. Pascha nostrum immolátus est Christus: ítaque epulémur in ázymis sinceritátis et veritátis.
content.english: ℣. Even Christ our Passover is sacrificed for us therefore let us keep the feast with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

segments.t: Pascha nostrum immolátus est Christus: ítaque epulémur in ázymis sinceritátis et veritátis.

content.latin: ℟. Et edent carnes et ázymos panes.
content.english: ℟. And they shall eat the flesh, and unleavened bread.

segments.t: Et edent carnes et ázymos panes.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.
content.english: Benediction. May the Son, the Sole-begotten, mercifully bless and keep us.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Unigénitus Dei Fílius nos benedícere et adiuváre dignétur.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 23 Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Iesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem,
content.english: 23 For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread.

segments.t: Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Iesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem,

content.latin: 24 Et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite, et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.
content.english: 24 And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.

segments.t: Et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite, et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.

content.latin: 25 Simíliter et cálicem, postquam cœnávit, dicens: Hic calix novum testaméntum est in meo sánguine: hoc fácite, quotiescúmque bibétis, in meam commemoratiónem.
content.english: 25 In like manner also the chalice, after he had supped, saying: This chalice is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as often as you shall drink, for the commemoration of me.

segments.t: Simíliter et cálicem, postquam cœnávit, dicens: Hic calix novum testaméntum est in meo sánguine: hoc fácite, quotiescúmque bibétis, in meam commemoratiónem.

content.latin: 26 Quotiescúmque enim manducábitis panem hunc, et cálicem bibétis, mortem Dómini annuntiábitis donec véniat.
content.english: 26 For as often as you shall eat this bread, and drink the chalice, you shall show the death of the Lord, until he come.

segments.t: Quotiescúmque enim manducábitis panem hunc, et cálicem bibétis, mortem Dómini annuntiábitis donec véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Comedétis carnes, et saturabímini pánibus:
content.english: ℟. Ye shall eat flesh, and shall be filled with bread.

segments.t: Comedétis carnes, et saturabímini pánibus:

content.latin: * Iste est panis, quem dedit vobis Dóminus ad vescéndum.
content.english: * This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.

content.latin: ℣. Non Móyses dedit vobis panem de cælo, sed Pater meus dat vobis panem de cælo verum.
content.english: ℣. Moses gave you not that Bread from heaven, but My Father giveth you the true Bread from heaven.

segments.t: Non Móyses dedit vobis panem de cælo, sed Pater meus dat vobis panem de cælo verum.

content.latin: ℟. Iste est panis, quem dedit vobis Dóminus ad vescéndum.
content.english: ℟. This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.

segments.t: Iste est panis, quem dedit vobis Dóminus ad vescéndum.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

segments.t: Iube, Dómine, benedícere.

content.latin: Benedictio. Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.
content.english: Benediction. May the grace of the Holy Spirit enlighten all our hearts and minds.

segments.t: Benedictio.
Spíritus Sancti grátia illúminet sensus et corda nostra.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: 27 Itaque quicúmque manducáverit panem hunc, vel bíberit cálicem Dómini indígne, reus erit córporis et sánguinis Dómini.
content.english: 27 Therefore whosoever shall eat this bread, or drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord.

segments.t: Itaque quicúmque manducáverit panem hunc, vel bíberit cálicem Dómini indígne, reus erit córporis et sánguinis Dómini.

content.latin: 28 Probet autem seípsum homo: et sic de pane illo edat, et de cálice bibat.
content.english: 28 But let a man prove himself: and so let him eat of that bread, and drink of the chalice.

segments.t: Probet autem seípsum homo: et sic de pane illo edat, et de cálice bibat.

content.latin: 29 Qui enim mandúcat et bibit indígne, iudícium sibi mandúcat et bibit, non diiúdicans corpus Dómini.
content.english: 29 For he that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.

segments.t: Qui enim mandúcat et bibit indígne, iudícium sibi mandúcat et bibit, non diiúdicans corpus Dómini.

content.latin: 30 Ideo inter vos multi infírmi et imbecílles, et dórmiunt multi.
content.english: 30 Therefore are there many infirm and weak among you, and many sleep.

segments.t: Ideo inter vos multi infírmi et imbecílles, et dórmiunt multi.

content.latin: 31 Quod, si nosmetípsos diiudicarémus, non útique iudicarémur.
content.english: 31 But if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.

segments.t: Quod, si nosmetípsos diiudicarémus, non útique iudicarémur.

content.latin: 32 Dum iudicámur autem, a Dómino corrípimur, ut non cum hoc mundo damnémur.
content.english: 32 But whilst we are judged, we are chastised by the Lord, that we be not condemned with this world.

segments.t: Dum iudicámur autem, a Dómino corrípimur, ut non cum hoc mundo damnémur.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℟. Respéxit Elías ad caput suum subcinerícium panem: qui surgens comédit et bibit:
content.english: ℟. Elijah looked, and, behold, there was a cake baken on the coals at his head, and he arose, and did eat and drink;

segments.t: Respéxit Elías ad caput suum subcinerícium panem: qui surgens comédit et bibit:

content.latin: * Et ambulávit in fortitúdine cibi illíus usque ad montem Dei.
content.english: * And went in the strength of that meat [forty days and forty nights] unto the mount of God.

content.latin: ℣. Si quis manducáverit ex hoc pane, vivet in ætérnum.
content.english: ℣. If any man eat of this Bread, he shall live for ever.

segments.t: Si quis manducáverit ex hoc pane, vivet in ætérnum.

content.latin: ℟. Et ambulávit in fortitúdine cibi illíus usque ad montem Dei.
content.english: ℟. And went in the strength of that meat [forty days and forty nights] unto the mount of God.

segments.t: Et ambulávit in fortitúdine cibi illíus usque ad montem Dei.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Et ambulávit in fortitúdine cibi illíus usque ad montem Dei.
content.english: ℟. And went in the strength of that meat [forty days and forty nights] unto the mount of God.

segments.t: Et ambulávit in fortitúdine cibi illíus usque ad montem Dei.

content.latin: Nocturnus II
content.english: Nocturn II

segments.t: Nocturnus II

content.latin: Ant. Memor sit Dóminus * sacrifícii nostri: et holocáustum nostrum pingue fiat.
content.english: Ant. The Lord remember our offering, * and accept our burnt-sacrifice.

segments.t: Ant.
Memor sit Dóminus * sacrifícii nostri: et holocáustum nostrum pingue fiat.

content.latin: Psalmus 19 [4]
content.english: Psalm 19 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 19

content.latin: 19:2 Exáudiat te Dóminus in die tribulatiónis: * prótegat te nomen Dei Iacob.
content.english: 19:2 May the Lord hear thee in the day of tribulation: * may the name of the God of Jacob protect thee.

segments.t: Exáudiat te Dóminus in die tribulatiónis: * prótegat te nomen Dei Iacob.

content.latin: 19:3 Mittat tibi auxílium de sancto: * et de Sion tueátur te.
content.english: 19:3 May he send thee help from the sanctuary: * and defend thee out of Sion.

segments.t: Mittat tibi auxílium de sancto: * et de Sion tueátur te.

content.latin: 19:4 Memor sit omnis sacrifícii tui: * et holocáustum tuum pingue fiat.
content.english: 19:4 May he be mindful of all thy sacrifices: * and may thy whole burnt offering be made fat.

segments.t: Memor sit omnis sacrifícii tui: * et holocáustum tuum pingue fiat.

content.latin: 19:5 Tríbuat tibi secúndum cor tuum: * et omne consílium tuum confírmet.
content.english: 19:5 May he give thee according to thy own heart; * and confirm all thy counsels.

segments.t: Tríbuat tibi secúndum cor tuum: * et omne consílium tuum confírmet.

content.latin: 19:6 Lætábimur in salutári tuo: * et in nómine Dei nostri magnificábimur.
content.english: 19:6 We will rejoice in thy salvation; * and in the name of our God we shall be exalted.

segments.t: Lætábimur in salutári tuo: * et in nómine Dei nostri magnificábimur.

content.latin: 19:7 Ímpleat Dóminus omnes petitiónes tuas: * nunc cognóvi quóniam salvum fecit Dóminus Christum suum.
content.english: 19:7 The Lord fulfil all thy petitions: * now have I known that the Lord hath saved his anointed.

segments.t: Ímpleat Dóminus omnes petitiónes tuas: * nunc cognóvi quóniam salvum fecit Dóminus Christum suum.

content.latin: 19:7 Exáudiet illum de cælo sancto suo: * in potentátibus salus déxteræ eius.
content.english: 19:7 He will hear him from his holy heaven: * the salvation of his right hand is in powers.

segments.t: Exáudiet illum de cælo sancto suo: * in potentátibus salus déxteræ eius.

content.latin: 19:8 Hi in cúrribus, et hi in equis: * nos autem in nómine Dómini, Dei nostri invocábimus.
content.english: 19:8 Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: * but we will call upon the name of the Lord, our God.

segments.t: Hi in cúrribus, et hi in equis: * nos autem in nómine Dómini, Dei nostri invocábimus.

content.latin: 19:9 Ipsi obligáti sunt, et cecidérunt: * nos autem surréximus et erécti sumus.
content.english: 19:9 They are bound, and have fallen: * but we are risen, and are set upright.

segments.t: Ipsi obligáti sunt, et cecidérunt: * nos autem surréximus et erécti sumus.

content.latin: 19:10 Dómine, salvum fac regem: * et exáudi nos in die, qua invocavérimus te.
content.english: 19:10 O Lord, save the king: * and hear us in the day that we shall call upon thee.

segments.t: Dómine, salvum fac regem: * et exáudi nos in die, qua invocavérimus te.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.english: Ant. The Lord remember our offering, and accept our burnt-sacrifice.

segments.t: Ant.
Memor sit Dóminus sacrifícii nostri: et holocáustum nostrum pingue fiat.

content.latin: Ant. Parátur * nobis mensa Dómini advérsus omnes, qui tríbulant nos.
content.english: Ant. The Lord prepareth His Table before us * in the presence of our enemies.

segments.t: Ant.
Parátur * nobis mensa Dómini advérsus omnes, qui tríbulant nos.

content.latin: Psalmus 22 [5]
content.english: Psalm 22 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 22

content.latin: 22:1 Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
content.english: 22:1 The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. * He hath set me in a place of pasture.

segments.t: Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit: * in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.

content.latin: 22:2 Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.
content.english: 22:2 He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: * he hath converted my soul.

segments.t: Super aquam refectiónis educávit me: * ánimam meam convértit.

content.latin: 22:3 Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.
content.english: 22:3 He hath led me on the paths of justice, * for his own name’s sake.

segments.t: Dedúxit me super sémitas iustítiæ, * propter nomen suum.

content.latin: 22:4 Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.
content.english: 22:4 For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, * for thou art with me.

segments.t: Nam, et si ambulávero in médio umbræ mortis, non timébo mala: * quóniam tu mecum es.

content.latin: 22:4 Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.
content.english: 22:4 Thy rod and thy staff, * they have comforted me.

segments.t: Virga tua, et báculus tuus: * ipsa me consoláta sunt.

content.latin: 22:5 Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.
content.english: 22:5 Thou hast prepared a table before me * against them that afflict me.

segments.t: Parásti in conspéctu meo mensam, * advérsus eos, qui tríbulant me.

content.latin: 22:5 Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!
content.english: 22:5 Thou hast anointed my head with oil; * and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!

segments.t: Impinguásti in óleo caput meum: * et calix meus inébrians quam præclárus est!

content.latin: 22:6 Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
content.english: 22:6 And thy mercy will follow me * all the days of my life.

segments.t: Et misericórdia tua subsequétur me * ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:

content.latin: 22:6 Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 22:6 And that I may dwell in the house of the Lord * unto length of days.

segments.t: Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini, * in longitúdinem diérum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

Parátur nobis mensa Dómini advérsus omnes, qui tríbulant nos.

content.latin: Ant. In voce exsultatiónis * résonent epulántes in mensa Dómini.
content.english: Ant. Let them that keep holiday around the table of the Lord * make the voice of joy and praise to be heard [in the house of God.]

segments.t: Ant.
In voce exsultatiónis * résonent epulántes in mensa Dómini.

content.latin: Psalmus 41 [6]
content.english: Psalm 41 [6]

segments.t: Psalmus 41

content.latin: 41:2 Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.
content.english: 41:2 As the hart panteth after the fountains of water; * so my soul panteth after thee, O God.

segments.t: Quemádmodum desíderat cervus ad fontes aquárum: * ita desíderat ánima mea ad te, Deus.

content.latin: 41:3 Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?
content.english: 41:3 My soul hath thirsted after the strong living God; * when shall I come and appear before the face of God?

segments.t: Sitívit ánima mea ad Deum fortem vivum: * quando véniam, et apparébo ante fáciem Dei?

content.latin: 41:4 Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?
content.english: 41:4 My tears have been my bread day and night, * whilst it is said to me daily: Where is thy God?

segments.t: Fuérunt mihi lácrimæ meæ panes die ac nocte: * dum dícitur mihi cotídie: Ubi est Deus tuus?

content.latin: 41:5 Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.
content.english: 41:5 These things I remembered, and poured out my soul in me: * for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:

segments.t: Hæc recordátus sum, et effúdi in me ánimam meam: * quóniam transíbo in locum tabernáculi admirábilis, usque ad domum Dei.

content.latin: 41:5 In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.
content.english: 41:5 With the voice of joy and praise; * the noise of one feasting.

segments.t: In voce exsultatiónis, et confessiónis: * sonus epulántis.

content.latin: 41:6 Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:6 Why art thou sad, O my soul? * and why dost thou trouble me?

segments.t: Quare tristis es, ánima mea? * et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: 41:7 Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.
content.english: 41:7 My soul is troubled within myself: * therefore will I remember thee from the land of Jordan and Hermoniim, from the little hill.

segments.t: Ad meípsum ánima mea conturbáta est: * proptérea memor ero tui de terra Iordánis, et Hermóniim a monte módico.

content.latin: 41:8 Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.
content.english: 41:8 Deep calleth on deep, * at the noise of thy flood-gates.

segments.t: Abýssus abýssum ínvocat, * in voce cataractárum tuárum.

content.latin: 41:8 Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.
content.english: 41:8 All thy heights and thy billows * have passed over me.

segments.t: Ómnia excélsa tua, et fluctus tui * super me transiérunt.

content.latin: 41:9 In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.
content.english: 41:9 In the daytime the Lord hath commanded his mercy; * and a canticle to him in the night.

segments.t: In die mandávit Dóminus misericórdiam suam: * et nocte cánticum eius.

content.latin: 41:9 Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.
content.english: 41:9 With me is prayer to the God of my life. * I will say to God: Thou art my support.

segments.t: Apud me orátio Deo vitæ meæ, * dicam Deo: Suscéptor meus es.

content.latin: 41:10 Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
content.english: 41:10 Why hast thou forgotten me? * and why go I mourning, whilst my enemy afflicteth me?

segments.t: Quare oblítus es mei? * et quare contristátus incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?

content.latin: 41:11 Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.
content.english: 41:11 Whilst my bones are broken, * my enemies who trouble me have reproached me;

segments.t: Dum confringúntur ossa mea, * exprobravérunt mihi qui tríbulant me inimíci mei.

content.latin: 41:11 Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
content.english: 41:11 Whilst they say to me day by day: Where is thy God? * Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

segments.t: Dum dicunt mihi per síngulos dies: Ubi est Deus tuus? * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?

content.latin: 41:12 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
content.english: 41:12 Hope thou in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

segments.t: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.english: Absolution. May His loving-kindness and mercy help us, Who liveth and reigneth with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, world without end.

segments.t: Lectio iv in opusculo 57

content.latin: Imménsa divínæ largitátis benefícia, exhíbita pópulo christiáno, inæstimábilem ei cónferunt dignitátem. Neque enim est, aut fuit aliquándo tam grandis nátio, quæ hábeat deos appropinquántes sibi, sicut adest nobis Deus noster. Unigénitus síquidem Dei Fílius, suæ divinitátis volens nos esse partícipes, natúram nostram assúmpsit, ut hómines deos fáceret factus homo. Et hoc ínsuper, quod de nostro assúmpsit, totum nobis cóntulit ad salútem. Corpus namque suum pro nostra reconcilatióne in ara crucis hóstiam óbtulit Deo Patri, sánguinem suum fudit in prétium simul et lavácrum; ut redémpti a miserábili servitúte, a peccátis ómnibus mundarémur. Ut autem tanti benefícii iugis in nobis manéret memória, corpus suum in cibum, et sánguinem suum in potum, sub spécie panis et vini suméndum fidélibus derelíquit.
content.english: The immeasurable benefits, which the goodness of God hath bestowed on Christian people, have conferred on them also a dignity beyond all price. “For what nation is there so great, who hath gods so nigh unto them, as the Lord, our God, is unto us?” Deut. iv. 7. The Only-begotten Son of God, being pleased to make us “partakers of the Divine nature,” 2 Pet. i. 4, took our nature upon Him, being Himself made Man that He might make men gods. And all, as much of ours as He took, He applied to our salvation. On the Altar of the Cross He offered up His Body to God the Father as a sacrifice for our reconciliation He shed His Blood as the price whereby He redeemeth us from wretchedness and bondage, and the washing whereby He cleanseth us from all sin. And for a noble and abiding memorial of that so great work of His goodness, He hath left unto His faithful ones the Same His very Body for Meat, and the Same His very Blood for Drink, to be fed upon under the appearance of bread and wine.

content.latin: O pretiósum et admirándum convívium, salutíferum et omni suavitáte replétum! Quid enim hoc convívio pretiósius esse potest? in quo non carnes vitulórum et hircórum, ut olim in lege, sed nobis Christus suméndus propónitur verus Deus. Quid hoc Sacraménto mirabílius? In ipso namque panis et vinum in Christi corpus et sánguinem substantiáliter convertúntur; ideóque Christus, Deus et homo perféctus, sub módici panis et vini spécie continétur. Manducátur ítaque a fidélibus, sed mínime lacerátur; quinímmo, divíso Sacraménto, sub quálibet divisiónis partícula ínteger persevérat. Accidéntia autem sine subiécto in eódem subsístunt, ut fides locum hábeat, dum visíbile invisibíliter súmitur aliéna spécie occultátum; et sensus a deceptióne reddántur immúnes, qui de accidéntibus iúdicant sibi notis.
content.english: How precious a thing then, how marvelous, how health-giving, how furnished with all dainties, is the Supper [of the Lord!] Than His Supper can anything be more precious? Therein there is put before us for meat, not, as of old time, the flesh of bulls and of goats, but Christ Himself, our very God. Than this Sacrament can anything be more marvelous? Therein it cometh to pass that bread and wine are bread and wine no more, but in the stead thereof there is the Body and there is the Blood of Christ; that is to say, Christ Himself, Perfect God and Perfect Man, Christ Himself is there, under the appearance of a little bread and wine. His faithful ones eat Him, but He is not mangled; nay, when [the veil which shroudeth Him in] this Sacrament is broken, in each broken piece thereof remaineth whole Christ Himself, Perfect God and Perfect Man. All that the senses can reach in this Sacrament, [look, taste, feel, smell, and the like, all these] abide of bread and wine, but the Thing is not bread and wine. And thus room is left for faith; Christ Who hath a Form That can be seen, is here taken and received not only unseen, but seeming to be bread and wine, and the senses, which judge by the wonted look, are warranted against error.

segments.t: O

content.latin: Nullum étiam sacraméntum est isto salúbrius, quo purgántur peccáta, virtútes augéntur, et mens ómnium spirituálium charísmatum abundántia impinguátur. Offértur in Ecclésia pro vivis et mórtuis, ut ómnibus prosit, quod est pro salúte ómnium institútum. Suavitátem dénique huius Sacraménti nullus exprímere súfficit, per quod spirituális dulcédo in suo fonte gustátur; et recólitur memória illíus, quam in sua passióne Christus monstrávit, excellentíssimæ caritátis. Unde, ut árctius huius caritátis imménsitas fidélium córdibus infigerétur, in última cena, quando Pascha cum discípulis celebráto, transitúrus erat de hoc mundo ad Patrem, hoc Sacraméntum instítuit, tamquam passiónis suæ memoriále perénne, figurárum véterum impletívum, miraculórum ab ipso factórum máximum; et de sua contristátis abséntia solátium singuláre relíquit.
content.english: Than this Sacrament can anything be more health-giving? Thereby are sins purged away, strength renewed, and the soul fed upon the fatness of spiritual gifts. This Supper is offered up in the Church both for the quick and dead it was ordained to the health of all, all get the good of it. Than this Sacrament can anything be more furnished with dainties The glorious sweetness thereof is of a truth such that no man can fully tell it. Therein ghostly comfort is sucked from its very well-head. Therein a memorial is made of that exceeding great love which Christ showed in time of His sufferings. It was in order that the boundless goodness of that His great love might be driven home into the hearts of His faithful ones, that when He had celebrated the Passover with His disciples, and the last Supper was ended, “the Lord Jesus, knowing that His hour was come that He should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved His own which were in the world, He loved them unto the end,” John xiii. 1, and instituted this Sacrament, this Sacrament, the everlasting “forth-showing of His death until He come again,” 1 Cor. xi. 26, this Sacrament, the embodied fulfilment of all the ancient types and figures, this Sacrament, the greatest miracle which He ever wrought, and the one mighty joy of them that now have sorrow, till He shall come again, and their heart shall rejoice, and their joy no man take from them. John xvi. 22.

segments.t: Tractatus 26 in Ioannem, sub finem

content.latin: Cum cibo et potu id áppetant hómines, ut neque esúriant, neque sítiant: hoc veráciter non præstat, nisi iste cibus et potus, qui eos, a quibus súmitur, immortáles et incorruptíbiles facit; id est, socíetas ipsa Sanctórum, ubi pax erit et únitas plena atque perfécta. Proptérea quippe, sicut étiam ante nos hoc intellexérunt hómines Dei, Dóminus noster Iesus Christus corpus et sánguinem suum in eis rebus commendávit, quæ ad unum áliquid redigúntur ex multis. Namque áliud in unum ex multis granis confícitur: áliud in unum ex multis ácinis cónfluit. Dénique iam expónit, quómodo id fiat, quod lóquitur; et quid sit manducáre corpus eius, et sánguinem bíbere.
content.english: By use of meat and drink men would fain that “they shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more,” Apoc. vii. 16, and yet there is but one Meat and one Drink, Which doth work in them that feed thereon that “this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal put on immortality,” 1 Cor. xv. 53, namely communion with that general assembly and Church of God's holy children, who are “kept in perfect peace,” Isa. xxvi. 3, and are “all one,” John xvii. 11, fully and utterly. And therefore it is, as men of God before our time have taken it, that our Lord Jesus Christ hath set before us His Body and His Blood in the likeness of things which, from being many, are reduced into one. In one loaf are many grains of corn, and one cup of wine the juice of many grapes. And now He giveth us to know how that which He spake cometh to pass, and how indeed “this Man can give us His Flesh to eat,” and His Blood to drink.

content.latin: Qui mandúcat carnem meam et bibit meum sánguinem, in me manet, et ego in illo. Hoc est ergo manducáre illam escam, et illum bíbere potum, in Christo manére, et illum manéntem in se habére. Ac per hoc, qui non manet in Christo, et in quo non manet Christus, proculdúbio nec mandúcat spiritáliter carnem eius, nec bibit eius sánguinem, licet carnáliter et visibíliter premat déntibus Sacraméntum córporis et sánguinis Christi: sed magis tantæ rei sacraméntum ad iudícium sibi mandúcat et bibit, quia immúndus præsúmpsit ad Christi accédere Sacraménta, quæ áliquis non digne sumit, nisi qui mundus est; de quibus dícitur: Beáti mundo corde, quóniam ipsi Deum vidébunt.
content.english: “He that eateth My Flesh, and drinketh My Blood, dwelleth in Me, and I in him.” To dwell in Christ, therefore, and to have Him dwelling in us, is to “eat of that Bread and drink of that Cup,” 1 Cor. xi. 28, and he which dwelleth not in Christ, and in whom Christ dwelleth not, without all doubt doth not spiritually eat His Flesh nor drink His Blood, although he do carnally and visibly press the Sacrament with his teeth but, contrariwise, he “eateth and drinketh damnation to himself,” because he dareth to draw nigh filthy to that secret and holy thing of Christ, whereunto none draweth nigh worthily, save he which is pure, even he which is of them concerning whom it is said: “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.” Matth. v. 8.

content.latin: Sicut, inquit, misit me vivens Pater, et ego vivo propter Patrem: et qui mandúcat me, et ipse vivet propter me. Ac si díceret: Ut ego vivam propter Patrem, id est, ad illum tamquam ad maiórem réferam vitam meam, exinanítio mea fecit, in qua me misit: ut autem quisquam vivat propter me, participátio facit, qua mandúcat me. Ego ítaque humiliátus vivo propter Patrem: ille eréctus vivit propter me. Si autem ita dictus est, Vivo propter Patrem, quia ipse de illo, non ille de ipso est; sine detriménto æqualitátis dictum est. Nec tamen dicéndo, Et qui mandúcat me, et ipse vivet propter me; eándem suam et nostram æqualitátem significávit, sed grátiam mediatóris osténdit.
content.english: “As the living Father hath sent Me, and I live by the Father, so he that eateth Me, even he shall live by Me.” This is as though He said: The Father hath sent Me into the world John x. 36, and I have emptied Myself [and taken upon Me the form of a servant, and being found in fashion as a man], Phil. ii. 7, 8. I have My life from the Father, as One That is greater than I. John xiv. 28. He that eateth Me, even he, by thereby taking part in Me, shall live by Me. It is as having humbled Myself Phil. ii. 8 that I live by the Father, but he that eateth Me, him will I raise up, John vi. 55, and so he shall live by Me. It is said “I live by the Father” that is to say, He is of the Father, not the Father of Him, and yet not so, but that the Father and the Son are co-equal together. Also it is said “So he that eateth Me, even he shall live by Me,” whereby He showeth the gracious work towards His people of Him Who is the “one Mediator between God and man,” 1 Tim. ii. 5, and not that He Which is eaten and he which eateth Him are co-equal together.

content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, spíritus, et ánimæ iustórum, Dómino: * benedícite, sancti, et húmiles corde, Dómino.

content.english: 3:74 O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless ye the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, Ananía, Azaría, Mísaël, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.english: 3:56 Blessed art thou, O Lord, in the firmament of heaven: * and worthy of praise, and glorious for ever.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli: * et laudábilis, et gloriósus, et superexaltátus in sǽcula.

content.english: Psalm 148 [5]

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

segments.t: Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

content.latin: 148:14 Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.
content.english: 148:14 A hymn to all his saints: to the children of Israel, a people approaching him.

segments.t: Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Vincénti dabo manna abscónditum, et nomen novum, allelúia.
content.english: Ant. To him that overcometh will I give of the hidden manna, and will give him a new name, alleluia.

segments.t: Ant.
Vincénti dabo manna abscónditum, et nomen novum, allelúia.

content.latin: Fratres: Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Iesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem, et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.
content.english: Brothers: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread. And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: Hymnus
content.english: Hymn

content.latin: Verbum supérnum pródiens,
content.english: The heav'nly Word proceeding forth,

content.latin: Nec Patris linquens déxteram,
content.english: Yet leaving not the Father's side,

content.latin: Ad opus suum éxiens,
content.english: And going to his work on earth

content.latin: Venit ad vitæ vésperam.
content.english: Had reached at length life's eventide.

content.latin: In mortem a discípulo
content.english: By false disciple to be given

content.latin: Suis tradéndus ǽmulis,
content.english: To foemen for his blood athirst,

content.latin: Prius in vitæ férculo
content.english: Himself, the living bread from heaven,

content.latin: Se trádidit discípulis.
content.english: He gave to his disciples first.

content.latin: Quibus sub bina spécie
content.english: To them he gave, in twofold kind,

content.latin: Carnem dedit et sánguinem;
content.english: His very flesh, his very blood:

content.latin: Ut dúplicis substántiæ
content.english: In love's own fullness thus designed

content.latin: Totum cibáret hóminem.
content.english: Of the whole man to be the food.

content.latin: Se nascens dedit sócium,
content.english: By birth, our fellow-man was he;

content.latin: Convéscens in edúlium,
content.english: Our meat, while sitting at the board;

content.latin: Se móriens in prétium,
content.english: He died, our ransomer to be;

content.latin: Se regnans dat in prǽmium.
content.english: He ever reigns, our great reward.

content.latin: O salutáris hóstia,
content.english: O saving victim, opening wide

segments.t: O
salutáris hóstia,

content.latin: Quæ cæli pandis óstium,
content.english: The gate of heaven to man below,

content.latin: Bella premunt hostília;
content.english: Our foes press on from every side,

content.latin: Da robur, fer auxílium.
content.english: Thine aid supply, thy strength bestow.

content.latin: Uni trinóque Dómino,
content.english: To thy great name be endless praise,

content.latin: Sit sempitérna glória:
content.english: Immortal Godhead, One in Three;

content.latin: Qui vitam sine término
content.english: O grant us endless length of days

content.latin: Nobis donet in pátria.
content.english: In our true native land, with thee.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Pósuit fines tuos pacem, allelúia.
content.english: ℣. He maketh peace in thy borders, alleluia.

content.latin: ℟. Et ádipe fruménti sátiat te, allelúia.
content.english: ℟. And filleth thee with the finest of wheat, alleluia.

segments.t: Et ádipe fruménti sátiat te, allelúia.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

segments.t: Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

segments.t: Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

segments.t: Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

segments.t: Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

segments.t: Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

segments.t: Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui nobis sub Sacraménto mirábili passiónis tuæ memóriam reliquísti: tríbue, quǽsumus, ita nos Córporis, et Sánguinis tui sacra mystéria venerári; ut redemptiónis tuæ fructum in nobis iúgiter sentiámus:
content.english: O God, under a marvelous sacrament you have left us the memorial of thy Passion; grant us, we beseech thee, so to venerate the sacred mysteries of thy Body and Blood, that we may ever perceive within us the fruit of thy Redemption.

content.latin: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Iam lucis orto sídere,
content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.latin: Deum precémur súpplices,
content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.latin: Deo Patri sit glória,
content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

segments.t: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

segments.t: Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

segments.t: Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

segments.t: Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

segments.t: Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

segments.t: Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

segments.t: Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 118(1-16)

content.latin: 118:1 (Aleph) Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.
content.english: 118:1 (Aleph) Blessed are the undefiled in the way, * who walk in the law of the Lord.

segments.t: 118:1 (Aleph)
Beáti immaculáti in via: * qui ámbulant in lege Dómini.

content.latin: 118:2 Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.
content.english: 118:2 Blessed are they that search his testimonies: * that seek him with their whole heart.

segments.t: Beáti, qui scrutántur testimónia eius: * in toto corde exquírunt eum.

content.latin: 118:3 Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.
content.english: 118:3 For they that work iniquity, * have not walked in his ways.

segments.t: Non enim qui operántur iniquitátem, * in viis eius ambulavérunt.

content.latin: 118:4 Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.
content.english: 118:4 Thou hast commanded * thy commandments to be kept most diligently.

segments.t: Tu mandásti * mandáta tua custodíri nimis.

content.latin: 118:5 Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!
content.english: 118:5 O! that my ways may be directed * to keep thy justifications.

segments.t: Útinam dirigántur viæ meæ, * ad custodiéndas iustificatiónes tuas!

content.latin: 118:6 Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:6 Then shall I not be confounded, * when I shall look into all thy commandments.

segments.t: Tunc non confúndar, * cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis.

content.latin: 118:7 Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.
content.english: 118:7 I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, * when I shall have learned the judgments of thy justice.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in directióne cordis: * in eo quod dídici iudícia iustítiæ tuæ.

content.latin: 118:8 Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.
content.english: 118:8 I will keep thy justifications: * O! do not thou utterly forsake me.

segments.t: Iustificatiónes tuas custódiam: * non me derelínquas usquequáque.

content.latin: 118:9 (Beth) In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:9 (Béth) By what doth a young man correct his way? * By observing thy words.

segments.t: In quo córrigit adolescéntior viam suam? * In custodiéndo sermónes tuos.

content.latin: 118:10 In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.
content.english: 118:10 With my whole heart have I sought after thee: * let me not stray from thy commandments.

segments.t: In toto corde meo exquisívi te: * ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis.

content.latin: 118:11 In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.
content.english: 118:11 Thy words have I hidden in my heart, * that I may not sin against thee.

segments.t: In corde meo abscóndi elóquia tua: * ut non peccem tibi.

content.latin: 118:12 Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.
content.english: 118:12 Blessed art thou, O Lord: * teach me thy justifications.

segments.t: Benedíctus es, Dómine: * doce me iustificatiónes tuas.

content.latin: 118:13 In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.
content.english: 118:13 With my lips * I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth.

segments.t: In lábiis meis, * pronuntiávi ómnia iudícia oris tui.

content.latin: 118:14 In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.
content.english: 118:14 I have been delighted in the way of thy testimonies, * as in all riches.

segments.t: In via testimoniórum tuórum delectátus sum, * sicut in ómnibus divítiis.

content.latin: 118:15 In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.
content.english: 118:15 I will meditate on thy commandments: * and I will consider thy ways.

segments.t: In mandátis tuis exercébor: * et considerábo vias tuas.

content.latin: 118:16 In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.
content.english: 118:16 I will think of thy justifications: * I will not forget thy words.

segments.t: In iustificatiónibus tuis meditábor: * non oblivíscar sermónes tuos.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
